Metadata.title: Roberto Zarzur | IT Manager & Software Engineer
Metadata.description: IT Manager and tech lead with a hands-on profile. I lead teams, build high-performance backends in Go, manage cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP) and ensure observability and DevOps in mission-critical systems.

About.title: About
About.mainTitle: From dev to manager without leaving the terminal
About.bio: I started as a full-stack developer and today I lead the technology area of a company with international operations. Along the way, I learned that true management requires hands-on involvement, which is why I continue to build backends, configure cloud infrastructure, and ensure that every system can handle production pressure. My delivery goes from code to final deployment.
About.bioExtended: I have delivered projects for Hospital Sírio-Libanês, Grupo Bandeirantes, and international hotel chains, always focusing on real performance, resilient infrastructure, and high-performing teams. My profile is hands-on: I code, review, configure infra, and make technical decisions on the same day.

band-news-bandsports.title: Grupo Bandeirantes
band-news-bandsports.shortDescription: Management of the complete refactoring of 6+ portals of Grupo Bandeirantes, modernizing the mass communication stack with zero downtime.
band-news-bandsports.description: I led the mission-critical technological modernization of the Band News, BandSports, Arte 1, Sabor e Arte, TerraViva, and Agro+ portals. I orchestrated design, engineering, and infrastructure teams while maintaining constant alignment with the group's C-Level. The migration included a strategic partnership with Vivo for content distribution.
band-news-bandsports.challenge: Modernize 6 mass communication portals simultaneously, without interrupting service for millions of users, coordinating multiple teams and maintaining architectural consistency.
band-news-bandsports.solution: Unified architecture in Next.js on the frontend and Go on the backend, with NestJS for auxiliary microservices. Edge security via AWS WAF, elastic Load Balancing, and gradual deployment with automated rollback.
band-news-bandsports.impact: 6 portals modernized with cutting-edge architecture, enterprise-grade security, and scale capacity for audience peaks (elections, live sporting events).
highlights: Direct coordination of Design, Frontend, Backend, and Infra teams
Migration of 6 portals without downtime
WAF and edge security configured on AWS
Constant alignment with directors and C-Level of Grupo Bandeirantes
Strategic partnership with Vivo for content distribution
Final stack: Next.js + Go + NestJS + AWS

caseStudy.problem: The Grupo Bandeirantes portals ran on legacy stacks with expensive maintenance, inconsistent performance, and difficulty scaling for audience peaks like elections and sports broadcasts.
caseStudy.solution: I designed a unified modern architecture that allowed each portal to be refactored with deployment independence while sharing core components. The Go + Next.js stack ensured maximum SSR performance with minimum latency.
caseStudy.robertoRole: I acted as technical manager: defined the architecture, coordinated 4 simultaneous squads, negotiated deadlines with the C-Level, and monitored every deployment. In critical sprints, I dove into the code to resolve performance bottlenecks.
keyDecisions: Choice of Go for the backend for throughput and latency
Adoption of gradual (canary) deployment to avoid downtime
AWS WAF for DDoS protection in high-audience events
lessonsLearned: Legacy system migration requires constant communication with non-technical stakeholders
Gradual deployment is non-negotiable for high-visibility systems
results: 6 portals modernized in an aggressive timeline

hospital-sirio-libanes.title: Hospital Sírio-Libanês
hospital-sirio-libanes.shortDescription: End-to-end architecture and engineering of the digital hospitality platform. Backend in Go processing 20M+ requests/month with 6ms latency.
hospital-sirio-libanes.description: I assumed full technical leadership of the backend, cloud infrastructure, and native app. I architected a high-availability platform for one of the largest hospital complexes in Latin America, including integration with the Tasy system, Unicast streaming with Widevine DRM, and an Android TV app in Kotlin.
hospital-sirio-libanes.challenge: Build a resilient platform capable of managing hospital operations in real-time, from content streaming to rooms to integration with hospital management systems (Tasy), all with near-zero latency.
hospital-sirio-libanes.solution: Backend in Go (Fiber) optimized for maximum throughput, with auto-scaling orchestration in GCP (Cloud Run). Distributed cache with Redis (92% hit rate), persistence in PostgreSQL, and observability via Prometheus. Native Kotlin app with Jetpack Compose and Media3 for Android TV.
hospital-sirio-libanes.impact: Stable production platform with 20M+ monthly requests, average latency of 6ms, and infrastructure ready for health audits and expansion to new hospital units.
highlights: 100% of backend and cloud built by me, no third parties
Go + Fiber: chosen for low latency and high throughput
Integration with Tasy hospital system for patient data
Unicast streaming with Widevine DRM (premium content protection)
Native Kotlin/Jetpack Compose app for Android TV
Monitoring with Prometheus and real-time alerts
Cloud Run with auto-scaling on GCP

caseStudy.problem: Sírio-Libanês needed a digital hospitality platform for its patients that integrated real-time information from Tasy, content streaming with DRM protection, and an intuitive interface on room TVs.
caseStudy.solution: I designed and built the entire stack: Go backend for maximum performance, GCP infrastructure with auto-scaling, Redis cache for instant responses, and Android TV app in Kotlin with Widevine DRM protected streaming.
caseStudy.robertoRole: I was the engineer responsible for the entire technical stack (backend, infra, mobile). Simultaneously, I acted as technical leader defining architecture, code standards, and monitoring. The decision to use Go came from the need for ultra-low latency in a hospital environment.
keyDecisions: Go + Fiber for performance: 6ms average latency
Redis as cache layer: 92% hit rate reduced load on PostgreSQL
Widevine DRM for premium content protection
Cloud Run for auto-scaling without managing servers
lessonsLearned: In healthcare, reliability comes before features
Observability is not optional. Prometheus saved nights of sleep
Integration with legacy systems (Tasy) requires obsessive documentation

fiesta-americana.title: Fiesta Americana Resort
fiesta-americana.shortDescription: Transnational management of a pioneering hospitality solution: convergence of Unicast streaming and coaxial broadcast on a single platform.
fiesta-americana.description: I led a global operation coordinating engineering teams distributed across multiple time zones. The project involved the creation of a native Kotlin app that does something unprecedented in the industry: simultaneously integrates cable TV signals (coaxial broadcast) and digital streaming (Unicast) in a single interface on the room's TV.
fiesta-americana.challenge: Enable an unprecedented hardware/software solution in the hospitality sector, aligning complex decoding engineering with management of stakeholders distributed across different continents and cultures.
fiesta-americana.solution: Cross-cultural project governance with communication adapted to each time zone. Engineering involving deep integration of hardware decoders (TV Box and USB dongles) with native Android TV frameworks, converging two transmission paradigms into a unified experience.
fiesta-americana.impact: Disruptive positioning of the hotel chain with a pioneering platform that converged previously isolated transmission technologies, creating a premium guest experience.
highlights: Teams distributed in multiple countries and time zones
Cross-cultural communication with international stakeholders
Total responsibility for deadlines, quality, and deliveries
Unprecedented solution: Unicast + Broadcast simultaneously in native app
Hardware integration: TV Box + coaxial signal via USB Dongle
Open and cable TV in the same hospitality app interface

caseStudy.problem: International hotel chains had two separate systems for TV: one for cable channels (coaxial) and another for digital streaming. Guests had to switch between TV inputs, creating a fragmented experience.
caseStudy.solution: I coordinated the development of a Kotlin app that decodes both signals simultaneously, presenting everything in a unified interface with integrated EPG. Hardware integration required custom drivers for USB dongles.
caseStudy.robertoRole: Complete management of the international project: alignment of stakeholders in multiple countries, roadmap definition, risk management, and quality assurance. My technical experience in Android TV was fundamental to validate architecture decisions.
keyDecisions: Use of USB dongles for coaxial signal capture (innovative solution)
Sprints adapted to different time zones
lessonsLearned: International projects require triple the documentation
Hardware integration has much longer test cycles than pure software
results: First app in the sector to converge broadcast + unicast
Successful deployment in international hotel chain

testimonial-2.quote: The platform Roberto built for us simply works. 20 million requests per month with 6ms latency, and he did it all alone, from backend to deployment. Exceptional professional.

testimonial-3.quote: Migrating 6 high-visibility portals without a single second of downtime is a technical and management feat. Roberto coordinated everything masterfully, maintaining clear communication with our C-Level at every stage.

Insights.title: Insights & Articles
Insights.subtitle: Reflections on technical leadership, system architecture, and the decisions that make a difference in production.

insight-1.title: Why your tech lead needs to code
insight-1.summary: Effective technical leadership requires hands-on involvement. Managers who abandon code lose critical context about the real complexity of the projects they manage.

insight-2.title: Go in production: what no one tells you
insight-2.summary: After running Go in systems that process 20M+ requests/month, I share the architecture decisions that made the difference and the errors that almost cost dearly.

insight-3.title: Observability is not a pretty dashboard
insight-3.summary: Prometheus, alerts, and metrics that really matter. How to set up an observability stack that only wakes you up when needed and lets you sleep the rest of the time.

insight-4.title: Multi-provider cloud: AWS + GCP in practice
insight-4.summary: Using AWS and GCP in the same ecosystem seems insane. But in certain scenarios, it's the smartest decision. I explain when it makes sense and how to avoid the problems.
